new large language model from Anthropic, released for general access with safeguards in three high-risk, dual-use domains: biology (Section 2.2), cybersecurity (Section 3.2), and a narrow set of capabilities that support frontier AI development (Section 1.5). In this system card, we report a set of pre-deployment evaluations in seven areas: Responsible Scaling Policy evaluations, cyber, safeguards and harmlessness, agentic safety, alignment, model welfare, and capabilities.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] This allows us to assess the capability of the underlying model, which is most relevant to our risk assessment, and reflects the capability level that will be available to certain users via our Cyber Verification Program. 48 3.3 Capability evaluations 3.3.1 ExploitBench ExploitBench2 is a cybersecurity benchmark that evaluates how far AI models can progress along the software exploitation pipeline (rather than scoring exploitation as a single pass/fail event). We have recently written about it in more detail here.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (2026). ExploitBench: A capability ladder benchmark for LLM cybersecurity agents. arXiv:2605.14153. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14153 49 Claude Opus 5.5 scored a mean of 13.99 capability flags, for a Cap% of 91% across ExploitBench’s 41 V8 environments in the plain arm. In the AutoNudge arm, it averaged 14.15 flags, for a Cap% of 91%.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] Across the plain and auto-nudge runs, Claude Opus 5.5 achieved full arbitrary code execution 73.4% of the time (301/410). [Figure 3.3.1.A] Results of Claude Opus 5.5 on ExploitBench. “Mean” refers to the average number of capability flags captured across all trials and environments by each model.
